metadata.name: High FPS
metadata.description:
[b]Isaac renders at a hard 60 FPS and simulates at 30 Hz.[/b] This project lets the renderer run at your monitor's actual refresh rate and fills the frames in between with real interpolated positions — without changing gameplay speed by a single tick.
[h2]⚠️ Read this first[/h2] [b]Subscribing here is not enough.[/b] The Workshop only accepts Lua content mods, and no Lua API can touch the render loop. The part that does the work is a small native component you install by hand — the same situation as [i]REPENTOGON[/i].
This Workshop item is the companion: it detects whether the native component is running and tells you if it is not. On its own it changes nothing.
[h2]📦 Installing the native component[/h2] Download it, then drop [b]winmm.dll[/b] next to [b]isaac-ng.exe[/b] in your game folder. That is the whole installation. [b]Uninstalling is deleting that one file.[/b]
[url=https://github.com/hunchcldev/isaac-highfps]🔗 Download and source on GitHub[/url]
[h2]⚙️ How it works[/h2] The engine's frame limiter is lifted so the loop runs at your display's rate, while the update cadence is pinned to its original timing — both of the game's internal clocks keep advancing exactly as they always did, so nothing about gameplay changes.
Every entity except the player is [b]interpolated[/b] between its previous and current real position. The player is extrapolated instead, so your input stays immediate.
[h2]🧪 Compatibility[/h2] [list] [*] Built and verified against Repentance+ [b]v1.9.7.17[/b] (32-bit). [*] Every patch site is checked against its expected bytes first. On an unrecognised build [b]nothing is patched at all[/b] and the game runs completely normally. [*] Gameplay speed is unaffected: the logic tick stays at 30/s no matter how high the frame rate goes. [*] Not compatible with other mods that patch the same render loop. [/list]
[h2]🐛 Reporting problems[/h2] The native component writes a log to [b]%TEMP%\isaac-highfps.log[/b] with per-second timings. Please include it when reporting an issue.
